text.p: Italian bond futures started lower in a fall-out reaction to French parliamentary elections on Sunday where the Socialist left won an upset victory, but they will need the support of the Communists for an overall majority.

Dealers said the election result highlighted the uncertainties over progress towards Europe's single currency already thrown into some doubt by Germany's internal row on revaluating its gold reserves to meet the Maastricht criteria.
"The French victory puts the whole EMU issue back into the melting pot, and any uncertainties here are very unsettling for the Italian market," said one LIFFE trader.

Dealers pointed out that the French Socialists were committed to launching the single currency, but they were demanding a flexible interpretation of the Maastricht treaty and early membership for Italy, Spain and Portugal.
"The danger is that EMU will be delayed or weakened, or both," said another trader on the LIFFE market.

Dealers said there was little reaction to the speech by Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio on Saturday, who said he was ready to gradually ease monetary policy but would tighten if necessary. He was speaking to the central bank's annual assembly.
